new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive and realized as high pitch; the high-pitched (stressed) syllable is the word-initial syllable in every polysyllabic word. In words of four or more syllables the high pitch extends rightward from the first syllable through the antepenult (2nd syllable in quadrisyllables, 3rd in longer words), the last two syllables being low. Monosyllables show no contrast.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described as such; instead 'spreading' of the initial high pitch to the 2nd/3rd syllable (up to the antepenult) in words of 4+ syllables.
new_statements.exceptions: Monosyllabic words excluded from the rule; high pitch is additionally used at phrase/sentence level to accentuate words for emphasis (sec. 2.3.3 Intonation); consonant length (gemination) is separately fixed on the penult of perfect verbs.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level rule stated on isolated words (citation forms, examples p.58 grouped by syllable count); author treats stress and pitch as one phenomenon (stress recognized only via high pitch); intonation handled separately. Impressionistic MA thesis with one main informant (Getahun Bogale). Note that Goldenberg 1968:68-69 (snippet only) describes prominence in terms of length vs. higher pitch with primary/secondary degrees and cites šabál 'wedding' with last syllable stressed and first higher-pitched, and Hetzron 1977/1997 call Soddo stress non-distinctive - so the initial-high-pitch analysis is one author's reading, not yet corroborated by a second primary source I could open.
new_statements.identity_note: Tesfaye Sima 1986 describes Kistaninya proper (= Soddo/Kistane, Northern Gurage of the Christian Soddo; informant Getahun Bogale), i.e. kist1241 itself. sources.note: Sec. 2.3 Suprasegmentals (p.55), 2.3.2 Pitch & Stress (pp.57-59), summary (p.67): Kistaninya is non-tonal; pitch and stress are only phonetic, fixed and predictable; high pitch = exponent of stress, fixed on the initial syllable of all non-monosyllabic words, spreading to the 2nd (quadrisyllables) and 3rd (longer words) syllable, i.e. through the antepenult; rule (7) S -> [+stress] / # __ (s(s))s s #. Examples p.58 with accent marks (mórä 'near', dáfa 'cause', ámäd 'ash').
